------ Forwarded message --------
From: Amy Malessa <[contact omitted]>
Date: Thu, Mar 18, 2021 at 11:39 AM
Subject: Quick After Action on Platform Accountability: What's Our Role?
To: Joshua Machleder <[contact omitted]>
Cc: Nadereh Lee <[contact omitted]>, Adam Kaplan <[contact omitted]>
Hey Josh,
Thanks so much for organizing this morning's webinar! I really enjoyed it.
I can see why people are skeptical and/or intimidated by this topic as a whole. So, how do we break it down more?
In hindsight, I probably should have focused less on past examples in Myanmar and Bosnia (which to be intellectually honest required an immense amount of effort
and political pressure to pull off) and more on smaller, concrete things that USAID officers can do in the future, like:
- Research to see what local laws and regulations governments already have on the books (or are considering) related to platforms.
- Figure out if anyone at your Mission already has contacts with platforms in the country or the region where you work.
- Identify local civil society organizations who are already working to hold platforms more accountable.
- Support existing or new forums that bring together government, civil society and platforms to discuss platform governance.
- What else am I missing? In terms of low-hanging fruit to get people started?
+ Nadereh and Adam, please chime in too based on your experience.In case this is useful for future sessions on the Disinformation Primer and also for us at OTI
since our projects have smaller timeframes and budgets.
Best,
Amy Noreuil Malessa
Senior Digital Technology Advisor for Field Programs Division
Bureau for Conflict Prevention and Stabilization | Office of Transition Initiatives | Creative Digital Team
